message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.37","text":"Some of our companions associate with Simon under false pretenses, as though they had been persuaded by his most godless error, so that by learning his plans they may disclose them to us, enabling us to adjust ourselves suitably to a formidable man. And now I have learned from them the subject of the debate about which he intends to deliver his arguments. Upon learning it, I thanked God and called you blessed because of the debate’s postponement; for before the debate, having been equipped by me in advance with the arguments that he is going to present for the testing of those who do not know, you will be able to become a hearer who does not stumble.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προσποιητῶς σύνεισιν","chosen":"associate ... under false pretenses","rationale":"The adverb indicates that their apparent agreement with Simon is feigned."},{"source_quote":"τῇ ἀθεωτάτῃ αὐτοῦ πλάνῃ","chosen":"his most godless error","rationale":"The superlative ἀθεωτάτῃ is retained rather than weakened to merely “impious.”"},{"source_quote":"δεινῷ ἀνδρὶ οἰκείως συναρμόσασθαι","chosen":"adjust ourselves suitably to a formidable man","rationale":"συναρμόζομαι presents an image of fitting or adapting oneself; δεινός here may mean formidable, dangerous, or highly capable."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἀγνοούντων","chosen":"for the testing of those who do not know","rationale":"διάκρισις may denote testing, discrimination, or separation; “testing” fits the surrounding account of deceptive passages functioning as a trial."},{"source_quote":"ἄπτωτος ἀκροατὴς","chosen":"a hearer who does not stumble","rationale":"This preserves the image of remaining unfallen rather than reducing it to being merely attentive or unconvinced."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.38","text":"For the writings acquired many false statements against God for the following reason: when the prophet Moses, by God’s counsel, had handed down the law together with its interpretations to a certain group of seventy chosen men, so that they in turn might equip those among the people who wished to be equipped, not long afterward the law, once put in writing, acquired some false statements against the sole God, who created heaven and earth and everything in them, because the evil one dared to bring this about for a certain just reason. And this happened with reason and judgment, so that it might be revealed which people dare fondly to accept the things written against God, and which, out of affection for him, not only disbelieve the things said against him but refuse to endure even hearing them at all, even if those statements should happen to be true, judging it much safer to take a risk for reverent faith than to live with a troubled conscience because of blasphemous statements.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αἱ γραφαὶ","chosen":"the writings","rationale":"The phrase denotes the authoritative written corpus under discussion without importing the boundaries or capitalization of a later canon."},{"source_quote":"γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"by God’s counsel","rationale":"γνώμη can mean judgment, purpose, decision, or counsel; “counsel” fits Moses’ authorized transmission of the law."},{"source_quote":"ἐκλεκτοῖς τισὶν ἑβδομήκοντα","chosen":"a certain group of seventy chosen men","rationale":"This preserves both the number and the indefinite force of τισίν."},{"source_quote":"δικαίῳ τινὶ λόγῳ","chosen":"for a certain just reason","rationale":"The phrase grammatically accompanies the evil one’s action; the rendering preserves that difficult claim rather than transferring the justification to another agent."},{"source_quote":"φιληκόως ἔχειν","chosen":"fondly to accept","rationale":"The adverb conveys affectionate or willing attachment, not mere intellectual assent."},{"source_quote":"κἂν ἀληθῆ τυγχάνῃ","chosen":"even if those statements should happen to be true","rationale":"The neuter plural predicate may take the singular verb in Greek. The startling concession is retained without theological harmonization."},{"source_quote":"περὶ εὐφήμου πίστεως κινδυνεύειν","chosen":"to take a risk for reverent faith","rationale":"εὔφημος contrasts reverent or favorable speech about God with the blasphemous statements that follow; an alternative is “to risk error for faith that speaks well of God.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.39","text":"Simon, then, as I learn, intends to come into the midst and recite the very passages against God that were added to the writings for the sake of testing, so that he may be able to detach from affection for God as many wretched people as he can. For we do not wish to say publicly that these passages have been added to the books, since by frightening unlearned crowds we would be doing the will of the wicked Simon himself. Because they do not yet possess the ability to discern, they will either flee from us as impious or, supposing that falsity is not confined to the blasphemous passages, withdraw from the teaching. We are therefore compelled, while assenting to the false passages and questioning him in return about them, to bring him into perplexity, but privately to furnish the solution, after a test of faith, to those who judge sensibly concerning the passages spoken against God. That solution has a single, brief path. It is this:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πειρασμοῦ χάριν προσκειμένας","chosen":"added ... for the sake of testing","rationale":"πρόσκειμαι indicates that the passages are additions, while πειρασμός here denotes a trial or test."},{"source_quote":"ἐλθὼν εἰς μέσον λέγειν","chosen":"come into the midst and recite","rationale":"The rendering preserves the spatial image of appearing before the assembled public rather than replacing it simply with “publish.”"},{"source_quote":"πτύραντες ἀμαθεῖς ὄχλους","chosen":"by frightening unlearned crowds","rationale":"πτύρω means to frighten or alarm; ἀμαθής describes those lacking instruction or learning."},{"source_quote":"ἢ ὡς οὐ μόνον τῶν βλασφήμων περικοπῶν ψευδῶν οὐσῶν ἀποστήσονται τοῦ λόγου","chosen":"or, supposing that falsity is not confined to the blasphemous passages, withdraw from the teaching","rationale":"The unexpressed counterpart to οὐ μόνον is understood contextually: hearers may infer that the larger teaching, not merely the offensive passages, is false. A more formally literal alternative is “or, as though not only the blasphemous passages were false, they will withdraw from the word.”"},{"source_quote":"συγκατατιθέμενοι ταῖς ψευδέσι περικοπαῖς","chosen":"while assenting to the false passages","rationale":"The speakers provisionally accept the passages as the basis of debate; the wording does not say that they affirm the passages as true."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ εὐγνωμονοῦσιν τῶν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ῥηθεισῶν περικοπῶν","chosen":"to those who judge sensibly concerning the passages spoken against God","rationale":"εὐγνωμονέω denotes sound or fair judgment; the genitive is taken as specifying the passages about which they judge."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἢ ὡς οὐ μόνον τῶν βλασφήμων περικοπῶν ψευδῶν οὐσῶν ἀποστήσονται τοῦ λόγου","issue":"The coordination is elliptical because οὐ μόνον has no expressed corresponding member. The contextual rendering understands an implied extension of falsity from the blasphemous passages to the teaching more broadly; the supplied wording is retained and admits a defensible translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.40","text":"Everything said or written against God is false. That we say this truly, not merely for reverence’s sake but also for truth’s, I will establish fully as the discussion proceeds a little farther. Therefore you, my dearest Clement, ought not to be grieved that Simon has postponed the debate for this one day—the present day. For since today, before the debate, you are being equipped in advance concerning the passages added to the writings, you ought not to be thrown into doubt during the debate concerning the sole and good God, who also made the world. Instead, during the debate you will also marvel at how the impious pass over the many things said in the writings on God’s behalf, yet look over the things said against him and bring them forward with delight. Thus the hearers, because of ignorance, believe the things said against God and become excluded from his kingdom. Therefore, having learned the mystery of the writings on the occasion of the postponement and having gained the benefit of not sinning against God, you will find gratification beyond compare.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐφημίας ἕνεκεν","chosen":"for reverence’s sake","rationale":"εὐφημία here concerns speaking reverently or favorably of God, in contrast with the surrounding language of blasphemy."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ βραχὺ προϊόντος τοῦ λόγου πληροφορήσω","chosen":"I will establish fully as the discussion proceeds a little farther","rationale":"πληροφορέω conveys bringing to full assurance or establishing fully; λόγος here is the developing discussion."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τοῦ μόνου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"concerning the sole and good God","rationale":"The rendering keeps μόνος and ἀγαθός as coordinated descriptions of God. “The only God, who is good” is also possible, but “the only one who is good” would alter their relation."},{"source_quote":"διακριθῆναι","chosen":"to be thrown into doubt","rationale":"In this context διακρίνω denotes wavering or divided judgment; alternatives include “to waver” and “to become uncertain.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰ πλήθη τῶν ὑπὲρ θεοῦ εἰρημένων","chosen":"the many things said ... on God’s behalf","rationale":"The idiomatic English preserves the contrast between the abundant favorable statements and the selectively cited statements against God."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει ὑπερθέσεως","chosen":"on the occasion of the postponement","rationale":"πρόφασις can mean occasion, stated reason, or pretext; “occasion” fits the delay serving as the opportunity for instruction without asserting deception."},{"source_quote":"ἀπαραβλήτως χαρίσῃ","chosen":"you will find gratification beyond compare","rationale":"The supplied χαρίσῃ is read as a future middle conveying personal gratification or pleasure. An active sense such as “you will grant incomparable favor” would leave its recipient or object unexpressed."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀπαραβλήτως χαρίσῃ","issue":"The supplied χαρίσῃ permits a contextually defensible future-middle sense, “you will find gratification,” but it is semantically unusual without an expressed object or recipient. The conjecture χαρήσῃ would straightforwardly mean “you will rejoice,” but that reading is not adopted in the translation.","proposed_reading":"χαρήσῃ","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
